title: Karrion Kross's One-Word Reaction to Sami Zayn Becoming WWE Undisputed Champion
htmlContent:
Sami Zayn walked into the triple-threat match for the Undisputed WWE Championship at Night of Champions in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, not knowing how the crowd would receive him if he won. He did not have to wait long to find out. In one of the most emotionally charged moments in recent WWE history, Zayn slipped out of a second Cross Rhodes attempt from defending champion Cody Rhodes, rolled him up, and got the three count, setting off an eruption inside the arena that reverberated far beyond the Kingdom.

For a man who has spent more than two decades grinding through the professional wrestling industry, the moment was not just a championship win. It was a vindication.

How the Moment Unfolded

The closing sequence of the triple-threat match was as dramatic as anything WWE has produced in recent memory. Cody Rhodes, fighting to retain his Undisputed WWE Championship against both Zayn and the imposing Gunther, lined both challengers up for his finishing maneuver, the Cross Rhodes. He connected on Zayn first, then redirected his focus to Gunther, sending him out of the ring before pulling Zayn back to the center of the mat for what appeared to be a match-ending second attempt.

But Zayn had other plans. He slipped out of the hold, spun behind Rhodes, and secured the rollup pin before anyone inside the arena fully processed what was happening. Referee Dan Engler counted to three, and just like that, the Last Real Good Guy had done it.

WWE broadcaster Michael Cole, rarely at a loss for words, summed it up in four: "A miracle in Riyadh."

Zayn's Emotional Response After 20-Plus Years

The image of Sami Zayn receiving the championship belt from referee Dan Engler, tears streaming down his face, the Riyadh crowd roaring around him, is one that will live in wrestling highlight reels for years to come. Zayn, never short on personality and rarely short on words, found himself momentarily speechless in the most important moment of his career.

When he finally spoke, he delivered one of the most honest and heartfelt championship speeches WWE fans have witnessed in recent memory. He acknowledged the critics, the doubters, and the years of being overlooked before planting his flag firmly in the moment.

"A lot has been said about me, some good and lately, some bad," Zayn said to Byron Saxton. . "A lot of folks said I would never win the WWE championship. But I stand here tonight in front of my people in Riyadh. It is hard to believe. Oh my God."

As fans chanted "You deserve it" throughout the arena, Zayn embraced every word.

"You know what? You're damn right I deserve it," he fired back. "Twenty-plus years in the game at the highest level — never got the recognition. Ten-plus years chasing this championship — never got the recognition. I don't care what happens to me tomorrow, next week, next month, next year. Forever, I will be Sami Zayn, WWE Champion."

With the win, Zayn also becomes the latest grand slam champion in WWE history, a milestone that further cements a career that has long deserved more recognition than it received.

Gunther's Rage and the Fallout Backstage

While Zayn was celebrating in the ring, chaos was breaking out backstage. Gunther, furious over the outcome, confronted SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis in a heated altercation that quickly turned physical. The confrontation hinted that the fallout from Night of Champions is far from over, and that Gunther, who views himself as the rightful champion, will not quietly accept this result.

Karrion Kross Reacts — and the Feud That Defined Zayn's Road to the Title

The reaction from the pro wrestling community was immediate and overwhelming, but one response stood out above the rest. Karrion Kross, who had one of the most psychologically layered feuds with Zayn throughout 2025, offered a single-word reaction at a question-and-answer session at Nickel City Comic Con in Buffalo, New York, alongside WWE legend and TNA Hall of Famer Mickie Jamesand his wife Scarlett Bordeauxat the Batavia Downs Gaming and Hotel on Sunday afternoon: "Finally," after the Wrestling With Emotion ‘Podcast’ delivered the news.

The word carried enormous weight given the history between the two. Kross spent the better part of 2025 attempting to push Zayn toward a darker, more ruthless version of himself, a slow-burning psychological feud that built across the year and culminated in singles matches at Night of Champions and SummerSlam. Their first singles bout at Night of Champions in Riyadh saw Zayn win, before Kross got his revenge on the July 21, 2025, episode of Raw.

By SummerSlam, the stakes were personal. If Kross won, Zayn had to publicly declare that Kross was right about him. If Zayn won, Kross had to admit he was wrong. It was one of the most compelling character-driven storylines WWE produced during that stretch — and Zayn came out the other side of it with his identity fully intact and his championship destiny confirmed.

A Champion the Business Needed

Sami Zayn's championship win at Night of Champions is more than a feel-good story; it is a statement about what professional wrestling rewards when it is operating at its best. Character, consistency, connection with the audience, and an unwavering commitment to the craft over two decades finally intersected in one rollup pin in Riyadh.

The miracle in Riyadh was twenty years in the making. And for Sami Zayn, it was worth every single one of them.

excerpt: Karrion Kross offered a single word — "Finally" — when asked about Sami Zayn's emotional Undisputed WWE Championship win at Night of Champions in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, capping a decades-long journey and a psychologically layered feud between the two in 2025.
